body.statement: When \(C_x\) has zeros or the anchor-zero subspace \(D_{a_s}\) is not contained in the range of \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\), characterize exactly which target directions admit two-sided observationally equivalent causal perturbations and determine whether point identification is equivalent to annihilation of the feasible two-sided tangent cone produced by the support-face route.
body.justification: Zeros in the common proxy kernel or an outcome support with deficient one-way tangent rank are the boundaries at which the division or two-sided support argument fails, so the tangent-rich theorem does not settle every sparse-proxy case.
body.gap: Neither the nonunique-bridge literature nor existing proxy bounds characterize the causal tangent cone of a fixed observed-law support face.
body.consumer: The answer would determine which exact-nullity conclusions survive sparse assay categories and structural zero outcomes instead of requiring artificial smoothing.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether annihilation of every fixed-completion two-sided support-face tangent space is sufficient for global point identification across all compatible latent representations.
obligation.obstruction: The support-face calculation is local and fixes a latent representation, whereas the compatible full-data fiber may have disconnected components with different proxy kernels, latent factorizations, or outcome support faces. No frozen assumption gives path connectedness or a theorem reducing global secants to local tangents.
obligation.attempted: The support-restricted signed-array equations were derived without division by proxy-kernel entries and both directions of the fixed-representation tangent characterization were checked. The remaining promotion was tested by a path-integration argument, which stops precisely because paths between arbitrary compatible completions are not guaranteed.
obligation.partial_result:
For a fixed compatible completion \(Q\), an exact computable local characterization is available.  Let \(\mathcal N_Q^{\pm}\) be the set of bridge increments \(h\), with \(h_0=0\), for which there are signed arrays \(\xi_{s,x,u,w}\) supported on \(\mathcal Y^+_{s,x,u,w}\) such that
\[
\sum_y\xi_{s,x,u,w}(y)=0,\qquad
d_{s,a}(x,u,w):=\sum_y\xi_{s,x,u,w}(y)y_a,
\]
and the following finite linear equations hold:
\[
\sum_u Q(U=u\mid Z_e=z,X=x,S=e)C_x(w\mid u)d_{e,a}(x,u,w)=0
\]
for every trial \(e\), assigned endpoint \(a\in\{l_e,r_e\}\), \(x,z,w\), and
\[
\sum_wC_x(w\mid u)\{d_{s,a}(x,u,w)-d_{s,0}(x,u,w)\}
=\sum_wC_x(w\mid u)h_a(w,x)
\]
for every \(s,x,u,a\).  These equations are well defined even when \(C_x(w\mid u)=0\), and support feasibility is computed by the range of the restricted marginal map \(\mathscr L_{s,x,u,w}\).  The set \(\mathcal N_Q^{\pm}\) is a linear subspace obtained by Gaussian elimination.  Every \(h\in\mathcal N_Q^{\pm}\) yields, for all sufficiently small positive and negative \(\varepsilon\), the kernels \(K+\varepsilon\xi\), which preserve every observed cell and the shared latent contrasts and change the target by \(\varepsilon R_0h\).  Conversely, differentiating any two-sided fixed-support perturbation that keeps the latent mixtures, proxy kernels, and assignment mechanism fixed gives exactly these equations.  Thus the fixed-\(Q\) locally attainable target-direction space is \(R_0\mathcal N_Q^{\pm}\), and local point identification along this route is equivalent to \(R_0\mathcal N_Q^{\pm}=\{0\}\).  What is not closed is the promotion of this local, fixed-representation criterion to global point identification over all compatible latent representations and disconnected support faces.
